title: Explicit Rate of Convergence O(log l / l) for Erdős #1014 k=3

problemStatement.plain: Prove an explicit quantitative rate bound for the convergence R(3,l+1)/R(3,l) → 1. While OQ-01 proved ε-δ convergence, this gives the concrete rate O(log l / l) with C = 2/c where c is the Kim-Shearer constant.
whyMatters: Strengthens OQ-01 convergence to a quantitative rate bound
Rate is sharp: recurrence forces O(l) increments, Kim-Shearer gives Θ(l²/log l) denominator
Universal rate O(log l / l) for all k ≥ 3 under conjectured asymptotics

proven: explicit_rate_k3: ∃ C > 0, ∃ L₀, ∀ l > L₀, |R(3,l+1)/R(3,l) - 1| ≤ C · log(l)/l
knownResults.goal: ACHIEVED: Explicit rate bound proved with C = 2/c

insights: Rate is sharp: recurrence gives O(l) increment, Kim-Shearer gives Θ(l²/log l), ratio is Θ(log l/l)
Key algebra: (l+1)·log l/(c·l²) ≤ 2l·log l/(c·l²) = (2/c)·log l/l for l ≥ 1
log²(l) < l for l large, via Mathlib's isLittleO_log_rpow_atTop with exponent 1/2
General-k convergence (without explicit rate) reduces to a 3-factor decomposition R'/R = (R'/g')·(g'/g)·(g/R), proved in parent's ratio_from_asymptotics
An explicit rate for general k is NOT extractable from the qualitative asymptotic hypothesis alone — it requires quantifying R(k,l)/g(l) → 1
